sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle, not a trend [F168].
Revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion, then rose 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [F5][D161][F6][D200][F7][D238].
The FY2022 jump came from higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, mostly from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Revenue then fell 20.5% in FY2023 on lower realized prices, and net income has declined three straight years to $8.0 billion in FY2025 [F8][D274][F20][D343].
Note that the table's revenue is a later recast, not the figure first reported: FY2025 shows $51.8 billion here against $58.9 billion in that year's 10-K [F10][X10].
The U.S. supplied 79.1% of FY2025 revenue and contributed 5.7pp of the 4.9% growth, while non-U.S. added 2.0pp [D382][D384][D342][D400].
Crude oil is the largest product line at 66.3% of FY2025 revenue but grew only 0.1%, contributing 0.1pp [D551][D552][D553].
FY2025 revenue rose on higher volumes of $6,197 million, including Marathon Oil volumes, partly offset by lower realized crude and bitumen prices of $4,615 million and $349 million [P28].
Net income fell 13.6% against revenue growth of 4.9%, so there was no operating leverage in FY2025 [D343][D342].
Basic EPS fell 18.7%, faster than net income, because the diluted share count rose 6.1% [D344][D356].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025, below the 17.9% window median and far under the 30.6% FY2022 high [F30][D831][D830].
Cost of revenue rose 11.6% against revenue growth of 4.9%, lifting its share of revenue to 37.9% from 36.6% [D352][D342][D326][D292].
DD&A rose $1,901 million in FY2025, mainly from the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes [P22].
SG&A fell $265 million, mainly from the absence of $545 million of Marathon transaction expenses in FY2024, partly offset by restructuring severance [P23].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.9% from 32.4%, widening the gap between operating and net margin [D332][D298].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, above the 2.18x of FY2024 [F59][F20][D333][D299].
The FY2025 decline in operating cash flow from $20.1 billion came from lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [P6].
Operating cash flow was 33.6% of revenue, and capex of $10.2 billion in FY2022 was 1.35x D&A [D331][F66][D228].
Free cash flow margin peaked at 24.1% in FY2021 against a 12.2% window median [D833][D834].
Net cash was $7.1 billion, or 12.1% of revenue, in the 100th percentile of six energy peers against a peer median of -7.7% [D337][D338][D850][D851].
FY2025 uses of cash were $12.6 billion of capital spending, $5.0 billion of buybacks, $4.0 billion of dividends and $0.9 billion of debt retirement, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sales [P7].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow, above the stated 30% framework [D339][F59][P31].
Return on average equity fell to 12.4%, below the 14.9% peer median [D341][D853].
The revenue basis break is the main data-quality flag: every year in the table is a recast below the first-reported figure, so growth rates mix presentations [R1][F10][X10].
Revenue fell 20.5% in FY2023 on lower realized commodity prices, partly offset by higher sales volumes [R2][D274][P47].
Net income has fallen for three years, from $18.7 billion in FY2022 to $8.0 billion in FY2025, a 24.7% three-year CAGR decline [F17][F20][D845].
Segment revenue members sum to 227% of consolidated revenue in FY2025, so they cannot be added [R4].
If net margin falls below the 15.4% FY2025 level toward the 8.1% peer median, the earnings downtrend would be confirmed in the FY2026 10-K [F30][D847].
If operating cash flow falls below the FY2025 $19.8 billion, the 46% payout would exceed the 30% framework and pressure buybacks [F59][P31].
If net cash falls below the FY2025 $7.1 billion, the peer-leading balance sheet would narrow, likely through the $5 billion disposition target or debt [D337][P32].
